g.text: '(' acts as a barrier | Inner-most bracket resolves first, then outer bracket, then pre-bracket operators
• Each '(' is pushed unconditionally as an isolation barrier.
• Next operators '-' and '+' see '(' on top → never pop past '(', pushed directly!
Precedence comparison stops at '('. Each bracket level executes in isolation.
Encounter first ')' → pop inner bracket, evaluate '2 + 10 = 12', then push '/' and '3'
Push 12. Pop inner '(' and discard. Stack now: [30, 6, 12]
Top is '-' : prec('/')=2 > prec('-')=1 → Push '/' directly!
Outer bracket expression now stands as: (6 - 12 / 3)
Encounter second ')' → pop until outer '(': evaluate '12 / 3 = 4' then '6 - 4 = 2'
→ Loop pops until matching outer '(' is reached:
Push 4. Operator top is now '-'. Operand stack is: [30, 6, 4]
Push 2. Operator top is outer '('. Operand stack is: [30, 2]
• Pop outer '(' and discard! Entire bracket expression evaluated to 2.
Remaining in operator stack: only the initial pre-bracket operator '/'!
See '*': equal priority to pre-bracket '/' triggers '30 / 2 = 15', then push '*' and '4'
Push 15. Operator stack becomes empty. Now push '*'!
Left-to-right rule: The '/' before the brackets evaluated with the bracket's result '2'!
End of String: Flush Remaining Operator '*' → Final Result 60
String ended. Flush remaining operator stack while ostack.size() > 0:
Push 60 to operand stack. Operator stack is empty → STOP!
else if (ch == ')') { while (ostack.peek() != '(') { pop op, v2, v1; push operation(v1, v2, op); } ostack.pop(); /* discard '(' */ }
